newsitem.title: INDIA: India opposition not to press no-confidence motion.
newsitem.headline: India opposition not to press no-confidence motion.

text.p: India's main opposition party on Thursday backtracked on a bid to topple Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, saying it would not press for a no-confidence vote against the government it had planned for Friday.

"We are not interested in a no-confidence motion early in the budget session," former prime minister Atal Behari Vajpayee, the leader of the biggest opposition group, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), told Reuters. "We want it as the last weapon."

Speaking after an address by President Shankar Dayal Sharma at the start of parliament's budget session for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), Vajpayee said the BJP had pursuaded a socialist ally to drop the no-trust move for the moment.
Asked if he expected Deve Gowda's 13-member alliance government to fall during the three-month long budget session, Vajpayee said: "It will survive for a while."

Parliament's lower house Speaker Purno Sangma had told reporters earlier on Thursday that he intended to take up the no-confidence motion by Samta Party leader George Fernandes for discussion on Friday.

But Samta party officials said they expected Fernandes to withdraw the move. Deve Gowda controls fewer than 200 deputies in the 545-member lower house but has the support of the Congress party which has about 140 seats in the Lok Sabha.
